# HR-003: the page writer kept overshooting the reading limit (prompt p2 to p3)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `age_reading_level` (limit 14 words per sentence at age 6). Follows [HR-001](HR-001.md), whose "what is still wrong" section named this.

## Trigger

After HR-001 the page-by-page writer in B1 was still over the limit on 22 of 224 first-pass pages (9.8%) in `sweep-2-p2`, against 4 of 224 (1.8%) for the one-call baseline. In the trace of one failing page (`a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f`, scene 7) the pages sat at 12, 14, 13 and 14 words and the failing one had 15. A second, smaller trigger: one story shipped with a note because the check counted "peach-colored" as one 13-letter word.

## Diagnosis

Hypothesis, written before the change: stating the limit made it the writer's target, and a model aiming at 14 overshoots by a word about one time in ten. A target two words under the limit should leave room. For the compound word: the long-word check should split on hyphens.

## Change

- Commit `05ca665` (Sat 10 Oct, Entire checkpoint `01M4JVWCZYN3VJVDYM070ZX1A8`): the page writer is told `limit - 2` (`target_sentence_words`); the verifier's limit is unchanged; the one-call baseline prompt is unchanged, so B0 stays a fair control. Prompt version `p2` to `p3`. The long-word check splits hyphenated compounds.
- Regression tests: `test_writer_prompts_state_the_reading_limit_the_verifier_enforces` (page writer gets the target, baseline gets the limit) and `test_hyphenated_compound_is_not_one_long_word`.

## Before and after

Same 14 jobs (7 drawings x 2 lessons, seed 1, arm B1, 5 workers). Before: the `sweep-2-p2` rows for those jobs (code `ffc4208`). After: `sweep-4-p3` ([report](../reports/20261010-1752-IST-sweep-4-p3.md), code `05ca665`). Outputs are sampled, so the stories differ between runs.

| | p2 | p3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pages over the limit on the first pass | 13 / 112 (11.6%) | **1 / 112 (0.9%)** |
| Stories with at least one such page | 9 / 14 | 1 / 14 |
| Repairs per story (mean) | 2.36 | 0.93 |
| Stories shipped with a broken promise | 0 / 14 | 1 / 14 |

- The one shipped-with-note story is the Mickey-1928 edge drawing, where `original_character_only` failed twice (a copyright edge case, not reading level).
- Seconds per story fell from 149.6 to 76.7, but fewer repairs and ordinary provider speed both contribute, so this is **not** claimed as an effect of the change.
- Traces for one job (bunny, sharing, B1, seed 1): p2 `a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f` (1 repair, 121.9 s); p3 `2776b05792e0e7ef1bc47f12bc6df571` (0 repairs, 55.9 s). Export: `evidence/traces/*sweep4-p3-bunny-sharing-B1.json`.
- Not measured: the effect of the hyphen fix on its own (the sample had no hyphenated compound failures); ages other than 6.

## Regression fixture

The two tests above; re-run job: `benign/bunny-bow-carrot`, lesson `sharing`, seed 1, B1.
E

# HR-004: a lesson saying "hurts trust" was a critical safety hit (neatlogs triage card)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `story_safe_text` (deterministic word lists on everything a child will read).

## Trigger

neatlogs's automatic triage opened card `ebcff17a` ("Overly restrictive deterministic blocklist in `verify:story_safe_text`", severity critical, confidence 0.70): a page whose feedback said "Pretending keeps a secret that hurts trust." was judged `critical` because of the word "hurts". Trace `26fbc879cddba411dc327286643276c3`; raw card in `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json`; the review of all three cards is in [TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md).

## Diagnosis

Checked against our code and the ledger, not taken on trust:

- Confirmed: `hurt`, `hurts`, `fight`, `fights`, `fighting`, `fought` were in `HARM_TERMS`, and any hit made the verdict `critical`, which the pipeline treats as "regenerate once, then stop" rather than "repair".
- Not confirmed: the card says the workflow halted ("`create-storybook` returning `null`"). A workflow span's output is always `null`, and no run in the ledger ended `stopped` (0 of 156 story runs), so no story actually stopped; the cost of a false hit was a page regenerated.
- A product that teaches honesty and sharing will use "hurts" and "fight" gently ("friends do not fight", "a secret that hurts trust"). A hard stop on those words is the wrong severity; a rewrite is the right one, which is what the module's own comment says ("a false alarm costs one repair").

## Change

- Commit `deb8f0d` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JW5XY38RXXWY9MMWWYDP7Z`): severe terms (kill, gun, knife, blood, weapon, bomb, death, punch, attack, gore, suicide and similar) stay `critical`; mild terms (hurt, hurts, fight, fights, fighting, fought) and unkind labels now give an ordinary `violation`, which means the page is rewritten. Instruction-steering text and personal data stay `critical`.

## Result

**Not supported, so the default is back to 90 s** (this commit). With the shorter timeout 12 calls were killed at about 37 s and the stories were slower; with 90 s no call stalled at all. Two readings fit and we cannot separate them: the provider was slow during sweep 5 (the average successful call was twice as slow) and the 40 s limit killed calls that would have finished, or hangs only appear at some times. Sweep 4 (90 s, earlier) also had no stalls, so the 87 s hangs in the triage traces were not reproduced in any of the 42 jobs we ran afterwards. Without a reproduction there is no evidence the change helps, and some that it can hurt, so we do not keep it. If hangs return, the better fix is probably a hedged retry (start a second call after a short wait and take the first answer), which needs its own experiment.

What the card was right about: the stalls are real and the timeout was the place to look. What it did not show: that shortening the timeout is safe.

Sample sizes are 14 jobs per arm and outputs are sampled; the cost estimates and the provider's state at the time are not controlled.

## Regression fixture

None: nothing was kept. The override `STORYBOUND_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S` stays so the experiment can be repeated.
